qt: to the Commission Christian Ehler (PPE), Andrea Wechsler (PPE), René Repasi (S&D) Subject:

The open public consultation on the Single Basic Act for Joint Undertakings1 and thematic priorities for the European Partnerships portfolio in Horizon Europe 2028-2034 will inform the accompanying impact assessment. Several mandatory items depart from standard survey practice and from the Better Regulation toolbox. Some questions require a single answer to what are really two (or more) separate questions. Respondents must rate in one answer whether partnerships support ‘development, uptake and/or deployment … by EU industry and society’ or whether ‘membership, participation, and funding access’ are ‘hard to understand and navigate’. Respondents are also asked to rate the effectiveness of something without specifying what they are effective at, e.g. ‘redesign rules for non-cash contributions’, ‘minimum size (budget) of call for proposals’, and even ‘other measures to improve flexibility in programming’. The scale runs from ‘extremely effective’ to ‘not effective’, with no option to say that a measure would actually be counterproductive. Joint Undertakings and Article 185 TFEU initiatives are grouped together throughout the survey, even though they have different governance and funding structures. Even if respondents reject a premise they must still rate its causes and remedies. 1.
Who methodologically validated this questionnaire before launch?
How will the Commission correct for these design effects when reporting results?
Will the microdata and the coding frame for open answers be published?
Council Regulation (EU) 2021/2085 of 19 November 2021 establishing the Joint Undertakings under Horizon Europe (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/2085/oj). 1
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.10.2026) The consultation questionnaire was prepared by Commission services, by the Commission’s Interservice Coordination Group established to oversee the work on the initiative and finally approved by the Secretariat-General1. In line with tool 53 of the Better Regulation framework (BRF)2, the consultation questionnaire strikes the right balance between closed and open questions. Open-text responses and additional targeted fieldwork will contextualise quantitative results, including where questions cover several issues or where respondents consider a measure counterproductive. If a measure is perceived as counterproductive, the respondent should select the ‘not effective’ option. Suggestions for actions with less adverse effects may be submitted in open-text replies and will be analysed and reported. In all questions there is an option to respond ‘Cannot Say’ or ‘I don’t know’. No rating will be applied, if these replies are chosen. The effectiveness of proposed measures is rated against the Single Basic Act objective specified in each question of Question group 4. The results will be reported based on the effectiveness of the proposed measures in reaching those objectives. Differences between Joint Undertakings and Article 185 Treaty on the functioning of the EU initiatives will also be considered in the analysis, notwithstanding their common treatment as Treaty-based partnerships for the purposes of the consultation. The Commission will publish all contributions to this consultation in accordance with the BRF, including a factual summary explaining how open answers were analysed. Respondents can choose whether they prefer to have their details published or to remain anonymous. The type of respondent, country of origin, organisation name and size, and its transparency register number, are always published.
1 On the review and approval of consultation documents, see European Commission, Better Regulation Toolbox,

December 2025, Tool #53, section 2.1, p. 475, and Tool #51, section 2.2, pp. 451–452. 2 https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-making-process/better-regulation/better-regulation-guidelines-andtoolbox_en.
